activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept of the atom (Dalton’ s atomic theory, Bohr’ s atomic theory, atomic mass and quantum theory)
suggested_methods: ICT based learning: Organise students to watch simulations, animations, videos or diagrams that illustrate the structure of an atom and write appropriate report
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of the atom is clearly described
suggested_resources: Pictures, diagrams, simulations, animations or videos illustrating the structure of an atom

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (b) Use different atomic theories to determine the electronic configuration of elements with different properties
suggested_methods: Interactive simulation: Guide students through interactive demonstrations, and explanations to explore the electronic configuration of elements with different properties
Peers coaching: Guide students to use different atomic theories to describe electronic configuration of elements with different properties and share to other students
activities.assessment_criteria: Electronic configuration of elements with different properties are clearly determined
suggested_resources: Pictures, wall charts and simulation illustrating the electronic configuration of elements

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explain the concept of chemical bonding and the interactions of atoms to form molecules
suggested_methods: Hands-on experience activities: Guide students to observe different materials with different types of chemical bonding and build models of different molecules using locally available materials
Group discussion: Guide students to discuss the interactions of atoms to form molecules and interpret the physical properties of different substances basing on their structures and bonding
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical bonding and interactions of atom to form molecules is clearly explained
suggested_resources: Molecular models, pictures, local materials, and video showing interactions of atoms

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (d) Describe the concept of gases in terms of the gas laws and the kinetic theory of gases
suggested_methods: ICT based learning: Guide students to visualise simulations and videos to describe the concept of gas laws and kinetic theory of gases and write a report
Experimentation: Guide students to perform experiments on the kinetic theory of gases
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of gases in terms of gas laws and the kinetic theory of gases is clearly described
suggested_resources: Diagrams, pictures, wall charts, simulations and videos illustrating gas laws and kinetic theory of gases
balloons, pollen grains, water, light source, microscope, thermometer, bicycle pump, heat source and bicycle tyres

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (e) Appreciate the applications of gas laws in daily life such as in fire extinguishers, aerosols, inflating tyres, bakery, liquefaction of gases and helium balloons
suggested_methods: Project: Task students to investigate the applications of gas laws and kinetic theory of gases in their environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Applications of gas laws in daily life are realised
suggested_resources: Bicycle pump, bicycle tyres, fire extinguisher, spray, balloons and NaHCO3

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements according to their positions in the periodic table
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explore the periodic trends of elements in the modern periodic table (Electronegativity, ionisation energy, electron affinity, atomic radius, melting point, and metallic character)
suggested_methods: Graphics method: Guide students to use graphic organisers to represent the periodic trends of elements in the modern periodic table
Inquiry-based learning: Guide students through explorations and asking questions to interpret the periodic trends of elements in the modern periodic table
activities.assessment_criteria: Periodic trends of elements in the modern periodic table are well described
suggested_resources: Pictures, wall charts of modern periodic table, and graphics programme demonstrating periodic trends of elements

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements according to their positions in the periodic table
activities.learning_activity: (b) Analyse the periodic trends of elements in relation to their physical and chemical properties
suggested_methods: Experimentation: Guide students to carry out experiments to analyse the periodic trends of elements in relation to their physical and chemical properties
activities.assessment_criteria: Periodic trends of elements in relation to their physical and chemical properties are analysed correctly
suggested_resources: Pictures, wall chart of modern periodic table, H2O, HCl, metal carbonates, HNO3, hydrides, chlorides, hydroxides of metals, oxides of Period 3, Bunsen burner, magnesium metal, sodium metal, calcium metal and electric current

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their applications in different contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept of colligative properties in understanding responses of the system towards changes in the environment (boiling point elevation, freezing point depression, osmotic pressure, relative lowering of vapour pressure and Raoult’ s law)
suggested_methods: Inquiry-based learning: Guide students through exploration and asking questions to describe different colligative properties in their environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Colligative properties are correctly described
suggested_resources: Thermometer, beaker, common salt, table sugar, weighing bottle, Beckman’s apparatus, Landsberger apparatus
osmometer, plastic bottle, analytical balance, freezing point apparatus, ethyl glycol, coolants and video showing colligative properties

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their applications in different contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Examine the applications of colligative properties in the purification of water, dialysis, preservation of food and in antifreeze and coolants
suggested_methods: Project: Task students to investigate the applications of colligative properties in industrial processes, automobiles and medicine
activities.assessment_criteria: The applications of the concept of colligative properties in the purification of water, dialysis, preservation of food and in antifreeze and coolants are clearly described
suggested_resources: Pictures, simulation, video, illustrating applications of colligative properties and coolants

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their applications in different contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Describe the concept of two component liquid systems (immiscible liquid, completely miscible liquid and the distribution law)
suggested_methods: Interactive simulation: Encourage students through interactive demonstration, explanations and hand-on activities to describe the properties of two component liquid systems
Experimentation: Guide students to carry out experiments on two component liquid systems
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of two component liquid systems is clearly described
suggested_resources: Separating funnel, beaker, immiscible and partially immiscible liquids, distillation apparatus, ideal and non-ideal solutions, side armed flask, fractionating column, thermometer, boiling flasks, condensers, pipettes, iodine, petroleum ether, burettes, flowers, leaves and propanone

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their applications in different contexts
activities.learning_activity: (d) Examine the applications of two component liquid systems in pharmaceutical industries and in the extraction of plant components, separation and purification of substances
suggested_methods: Problem-based learning: Create environment for students to explore the applications of two component liquid systems in solving real life scenarios in their environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Applications of two component liquid systems are well examined
suggested_resources: Pictures, video simulation, illustrating applications of two component liquid systems

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their applications in different contexts
activities.learning_activity: (e) Describe the concept of energetics (Heat/enthalpy of reactions and Hess’ s law)
suggested_methods: Group discussion: Guide students to discuss the concept of energetics
Experimentation: Guide students to carry out experiments on energetics
activities.assessment_criteria: The concepts of heat/ enthalpy of reactions and Hess’s law are clearly described
suggested_resources: Salts, acid, base, thermometer, analytical balance, magnesium ribbon, sodium thiosulphate, calorimeters, chemical indicators and simulation, illustrating energetics

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of chemical concepts and principles and their applications in different contexts
activities.learning_activity: (f) Examine the applications of energetics in daily life in combustion of fuel, cooking and human body metabolism
suggested_methods: Problem-solving method: Provide students with scenario or case study and task them to investigate the applications of energetics in their environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Applications of energetics in daily life are clearly examined and demonstrated
suggested_resources: Pictures, wall charts, video showing applications of energetics

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of advanced concepts and principles in organic chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concepts of aromatic hydrocarbons, halogen derivatives of hydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, amines and polymers
suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Guide students to use visual aids to describe the concepts of aromatic hydrocarbons, halogen derivatives of hydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, amines and polymers

Library search: Task students to read articles and present information on the health hazards associated with polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids, haloalkanes, amines and polymers
activities.assessment_criteria: The concepts of aromatic hydrocarbons, halogen derivatives of hydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, amines and polymers are clearly described
suggested_resources: Molecular models, visual aids and pictures, illustrating organic compounds, chemistry software, products made from organic compounds such as dyes, pesticides, detergents, artificial food flavor, rubber and medicine

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of advanced concepts and principles in organic chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (b) Apply IUPAC rules in naming of aromatic hydrocarbons, halohydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, and amines
suggested_methods: Inquiry-based learning: Guide students to explore the IUPAC rules for naming aromatic hydrocarbons, halohydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, and amines
activities.assessment_criteria: IUPAC rules of naming aromatic hydrocarbons, halohydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, and amines are well applied
suggested_resources: Chemistry software and containers with labelled organic compounds

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of advanced concepts and principles in organic chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (c) Examine reactions of aromatic hydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, and carboxylic acids and their derivatives for preparation of useful organic products like soaps, perfumes and pesticides
suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Guide students to use visual aids to explore the reactions of aromatic hydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds, and carboxylic acids and their derivatives
Practical works: Guide students to isolate essential oils from plant materials and spices, and carry out experiments on the preparations of soaps, perfumes and pesticides
activities.assessment_criteria: Reactions of aromatic hydrocarbons, phenols, carbonyl compounds and, carboxylic acids and their derivatives are properly examined and demonstrated
suggested_resources: Fragrances, alcohols, distillers, oil and fat, KOH/NaOH, glycerine, orange peels, lemon grass, ginger roots, rose flowers and other scented plant materials, laboratory note book and visual aids describing reactions for selected organic compounds

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.4 Demonstrate an understanding of advanced concepts and principles in organic chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (d) Examine reactions of haloalkanes, amines and polymers for preparation of useful organic products like plastics, dyes, detergents and rubber
suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Guide students to use visual aids to explore the reactions of haloalkanes, amines and polymers
Inquiry-based learning: Task students to search and present information related to structures and properties of polymeric materials used as adhesives, semiconductors packaging and insulators
Hands-on mind-on activities: Guide students to carry out experiments on the preparation of plastics, dyes, detergents and rubber
activities.assessment_criteria: Reactions of haloalkanes, amines and polymers are properly examined and demonstrated
suggested_resources: Starch, cellulose, vegetable oils, natural sources of dyes, plastic materials, food stuffs and visual aids showing reactions of haloalkanes, amines and polymers

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Conduct experiments in chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Conduct synthesis of selected organic compounds
activities.learning_activity: (a) Synthesise aromatic hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, amines and polymers
suggested_methods: Experimentation: Guide students to carry out laboratory experiments on the synthesis of aromatic hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, amines and polymers
activities.assessment_criteria: Aromatic hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, phenols, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and their derivatives, amines and polymers are synthesised
suggested_resources: Ethylene, caustic soda, sulfonic acid, perfume, water, selected apparatus/ equipment for organic reactions, chemistry software and laboratory notebook

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Conduct a project in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Conduct a project in Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (a) Design and carry out a project in Chemistry
suggested_methods: Project: Guide students to design a project from any Chemistry themes
Field trip: Task students to investigate the selected Chemistry theme and carry out the project
activities.assessment_criteria: The project is well designed and carried out
suggested_resources: Factories for production of different products, project guidelines, sample of project reports, laboratory facilities, and materials

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1. Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles of Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept of chemical equilibria in predicting the direction of reactions for formation of desired products (dynamic equilibrium, ionic equilibrium and acid-base equilibrium)
suggested_methods: Group discussion: Guide students to discuss the concept of chemical equilibria
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of chemical equilibria are clearly described

NH3, H2SO4, water, wood ash, lemons, acid,  bases, weak and strong acids
weak and strong bases, pH meter,
BaSO4, CaCO3, AgCl, AgNO3, Na2SO4, and Ba(NO3)2

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1. Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles of Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (b) Perform experiments involving chemical equilibria and report the experimental results scientifically (preparation of buffer solutions and acid-base titrations)
suggested_methods: Experimentation: Guide students to carry out experiments on dynamic equilibrium, ionic equilibrium and acid-base equilibrium
activities.assessment_criteria: Experiments involving chemical equilibria and experimental results are scientifically performed

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.1. Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles of Chemistry
activities.learning_activity: (c) Assess the applications of chemical equilibria in industries and daily life (manufacture of H2SO4, fertilizers, photochromic lenses and, acids, bases and salts in food industries)
suggested_methods: Problem-based learning: Task students to investigate the applications of chemical equilibria in industries and daily life
activities.assessment_criteria: Applications of chemical equilibria in industries and daily life are well assessed

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements according to their position in the periodic table

suggested_methods: Interactive simulation: Employ visual aids to guide students to describe physical and chemical properties of transition elements

finely divided first row transition elements and their chlorides, carbonates, sulphates, hydroxides and nitrates,

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements according to their position in the periodic table
activities.learning_activity: (b) Describe the concept of complex compounds (type of complexes and factors affecting complex formation)
suggested_methods: ICT based learning: Through interactive demonstrations, explanations and hands-on activities guide students to visualise simulations and describe the concept of complex formation
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of complex compounds is clearly described

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the concepts, theories and principles in Chemistry
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of changes in the physical and chemical properties of elements according to their position in the periodic table
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explore reactions of complex compounds
suggested_methods: Experimentation: Guide students to carry out experiments on the reactions of complex compounds and prepare scientific reports

activities.learning_activity: (a) Complete and submit for assessment a scientific  report of the project started in Form Five
suggested_methods: Practical: Guide students to perform experiments of the selected Chemistry themes started in    Form Five
Project: Guide students to  analyse the experimental data by using ICT facilities and submit the  synthesised product(s) and scientific report for assessment
